headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and parse tool outputs, while RD-Agent writes logs and uses browser/API workflows. A shared workspace or copied artifacts create a plausible injection bridge, but no direct shared channel is documented, so I rate it medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory or log directory, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF RD-Agent outputs are copied into CrewAI tool prompts without sanitization, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Disable automatic ingestion of logs or browser output into prompts.
Add a fixed allowlist for files each agent may read.
Insert a human review step before forwarding outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data and broad network egress; RD-Agent handles financial reports, datasets, execution traces, and logs, and also calls external APIs. If they share files or credentials, sensitive data can flow out through either agent’s outbound requests, but the profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default.
conditions: IF the same sensitive dataset is mounted into both agents, both can access it.
IF either agent is configured to send shared files to model APIs, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Use separate secrets and API keys per agent.
Mount only the minimum required files into each process.
Turn off network egress for nonessential runs.
Review logs for accidental data capture.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has write_filesystem and subprocess execution; RD-Agent has API access and file logging. Their capabilities overlap on mutable artifacts, so concurrent writes or log clobbering are plausible if they share a workspace. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file races can occur.
IF both agents update shared state without locks, one agent can overwrite the other's artifacts.
mitigations: Give each agent its own output directory.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Make shared artifacts read-only.
Check timestamps before overwriting files.
requires-engineering: add transactional state management.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration layer that can pass outputs between agents, and RD-Agent is a research automation system that can act on generated analyses and logs. If CrewAI forwards RD-Agent outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions; no built-in verification is shown, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF CrewAI uses RD-Agent outputs as inputs to tool calls without verification, errors propagate.
IF RD-Agent-generated claims are treated as facts in downstream automation, incorrect actions can follow.
mitigations: Require a verification step before any action.
Compare outputs against source files or datasets.
Flag low-confidence claims for review.
Limit automated actions to dry-run mode.
requires-engineering: add structured provenance and validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs, while CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and external tool/API secrets. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if the pair is used on regulated data, but the profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction or certification conflict, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated financial or personal data is processed through both agents, retention policy mismatch becomes relevant.
IF logs from RD-Agent are retained longer than the source data policy, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Classify the data before running either agent.
Set a short log-retention window.
Keep regulated data out of shared prompts.
Document which system is the record of truth.
requires-engineering: implement policy-aware retention controls.
